title: 2. First Council of Constantinople (381)
about: Is the Holy Spirit God? The council that completed the Creed.

items.text: After Nicaea some accepted the Son but taught that the Holy Spirit was a creature or a servant of God. In 381 the Emperor Theodosius gathered 150 bishops in Constantinople, with St Gregory the Theologian and St Gregory of Nyssa among them.
We are baptised into one Name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Lying to the Holy Spirit is lying to God (Acts 5:3-4).

days.title: St Basil on the Holy Spirit

items.text: St Basil died before the council, but his book On the Holy Spirit prepared the way. Read the first chapters on giving glory 'to the Father, with the Son, together with the Holy Spirit'.

items.father: St Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit

items.text: The council added the words on the Holy Spirit: 'the Lord, the Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified'. This is the Creed the Orthodox Church says today, with no additions. The council also condemned Apollinarius, who denied that Christ had a human mind.

items.father: The Creed and canons of the First Council of Constantinople

items.text: St Gregory's Fifth Theological Oration (Oration 31) is the classic sermon on the divinity of the Holy Spirit.
